question: Which stage of photosynthesis produces ATP but does NOT fix carbon?
citations: chunk:8_1_overview_of_photosynthesis_biology_2e_openstax:17 | data/8.1 Overview of Photosynthesis - Biology 2e _ OpenStax.pdf | 6/8 Figure 8.7 Photosynthesis takes place in two stages: light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle. Light-depend...
reasoning: Matched entities: atp, photosynthesis, 5-carbon sugar. Traversed graph edges: ATP synthase --[forms]--> ATP; ATP synthase --[attaches]--> a third phosphate group to ADP; Calvin cycle --[consumes]--> ATP. Graph evidence: "The energy released by the hydrogen ion stream allows ATP synthase to attach a third phosphate group to ADP, which forms a molecule of ATP (Figure 8.17).". The light-dependent reactions produce ATP and NADPH using light energy, while the Calvin cycle (which fixes carbon) uses the energy from these compounds to make G3P from CO2. Therefore, the light-dependent reactions produce ATP but do not fix carbon.
